motion.name: curtain
motion.purpose: Curtain halves travel 104% off the stage when the deck opens or a card is read.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: The reading sheet enters from 16px down, scale 0.98, and 8px of blur.

motion.name: hold
motion.purpose: One breath. Seven lamps light in even steps. At the end the closed stack translates -10px and scales to 1.04.

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: Cards spring from the fan into the ellipse. The loop settles when energy drops under 18, with a 1.7s fallback.

motion.name: orbit
motion.purpose: Slow orbit. A fine pointer slows it to 0.22×. Keyboard focus slows it to 0.4×.

motion.name: detent
motion.purpose: A short tick when the breath completes. A pick uses 10ms.

narrative.overview:
Cards of Answers is one paper toy theater on an otherwise empty field. A vermilion proscenium frames a plum interior, a violet curtain of pleats covers the opening, a cream apron holds the stage directions, and seven gold lamps mark a breath. The wordmark, the deck, and the apron are one object. The person brings a question they never type, presses the closed curtain, and releases when the lamps are lit. The curtain leaves, twenty-four illustrated cards spring into a slow orbit, and the chosen card becomes a cream sheet with its picture and one sentence.

The voice is split on purpose and then left alone. Anybody, a self-hosted variable sans, calls the arch, the stage directions, the category, and the controls, set a little condensed. Petrona, a self-hosted variable serif, speaks the answer and the instruction to hold. The illustrations are the existing flat category webps. The stage frames them. It does not repaint them. Density is one object, one answer, and a quiet status line.

Motion is one sequence, not a kit of entrances. The lamps fill across the hold, the curtain travels off, the cards spring and then orbit, and the sheet arrives once, from a short fall, a slight scale, and a blur. Reduced motion keeps the same cards and the same answer, drops the travel and the orbit, and lays the open deck out as a still grid. This world refuses the dark tarot page, the shuffle button, and a sentence shown without its picture.
keyCharacteristics: One theater, centered, filling the viewport
Plum field, vermilion frame, violet pleats, cream paper, gold lamps
Anybody for the call, Petrona for the line
Press-and-hold, then a pick, then the picture and the sentence together
Soft cast shadows, an inset cavity, and a fine noise on the field
A still grid when motion is reduced

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: Vermilion paints the proscenium, the kept-card stroke, text selection, and the form accent. It does not fill buttons, and it does not carry the answer.

rules.name: The Pleat Rule
rules.body: The curtain is three violet cloths, repeating light, pleat, shadow across seven folds a side. Category type and the apron focus ring use violet deep. The scrollbar uses violet fold. These violets do not stand in for vermilion or gold.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Anybody carries the arch, the stage directions, the category, and the controls. Petrona speaks the answer, the hold instruction, the date note, and status. The voices do not swap.

rules.name: The Condensed Arch Rule
rules.body: Anybody is condensed: width 92% on the wordmark, 94% on the stage direction, 98% on the category and the controls. It is not set wide.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: The wordmark, the stage, and the apron are one theater, centered on the plum field. A new surface joins that object. It does not sit beside it as a second panel.

rules.name: The Still Deck Rule
rules.body: When reduced motion is on, the orbit becomes a four-column grid, three columns below 720px. The curtain and the reading sheet do not travel. The same cards and the same answer stay reachable.

rules.name: The Three Depths Rule
rules.body: The field is plum, the theater interior is plum deep, and the stage opening is the cavity. Cream paper sits on that stack. Do not add another dark.

rules.name: The Soft Cast Rule
rules.body: The theater, the cards, and the reading sheet cast a soft shadow with offset and blur. A hard, unblurred offset shadow is not part of this stage.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: The apron and the reading sheet are flat cream. They do not lift, and they do not use a glass blur. The sheet’s one entrance is the only blur, and it clears.

rules.name: The Arch Rule
rules.body: The proscenium and the stage opening are elliptical arches, tall across the top and short along the bottom. Cards, the reading sheet, and the apron use small even corners. Controls are pills. Lamps are circles. The shared image stays a sharp rectangle.

rules.name: The Breath Rule
rules.body: The hold lasts 3.4 seconds and lights seven lamps. At full, the closed stack lifts 10px and scales to 1.04, the stage direction becomes Release, and an 18ms vibration marks the detent. Releasing early restores the stack and leaves the curtain closed. A pick uses a 10ms tick.

rules.name: The Sentence Arrives Rule
rules.body: The chosen illustration and its sentence arrive together on the cream sheet, in one motion. The picture is not dropped to leave a quotation.

rules.name: The Focus Rule
rules.body: Focus is a 2px ring, never a glow. Gold at a 3px offset is the default. A card uses cream at 4px. The press target uses gold at 6px. Apron controls use violet deep at 3px.

dos: Do keep the theater as one object: plum field, vermilion arch, violet pleats, cream apron, gold lamps.
Do set Anybody for the arch, the stage directions, the category, and the controls, and Petrona for the answer and the hold instruction.
Do self-host Anybody and Petrona from `site/fonts`, with sans-serif and Georgia only as fallbacks.
Do show the category illustration with the sentence, on the reading sheet and on the kept PNG, and leave the illustration’s own inks alone.
Do theme selection (vermilion ink behind cream type), focus (gold, cream on a card, violet deep on the apron), and the scrollbar (violet fold on plum deep) from this palette.
Do give reduced motion a still grid instead of the orbit, and keep the curtain and the reading sheet from animating.
donts: Don't add a shuffle control. The draw is a press-and-hold of one breath, then a pick.
Don't show the answer without its illustration.
Don't set the answer in Anybody, or the stage directions in Petrona.
Don't fill buttons or body text with vermilion, and don't set type in gold.
Don't use a hard offset shadow, or a second card chrome around the reading sheet.
Don't put a kicker above the stage direction or the answer. The heading is the line. The category sits under the sentence as the card’s name.
